grammar.title: Offer an action towards the recipient
grammar.formation: お + suitable verb ます-stem + する/します. For many Sino-Japanese する verbs use ご + verbal noun + する. Prefixes have lexical exceptions, including お電話する.
grammar.explanation: Describe an action by your own side towards a respected recipient: send something to them, hold their bag or let them know. The person being respected may be a third party, not necessarily the listener. Do not turn the recipient’s action into your humble action. Not every verb accepts this template: use an established special form where appropriate, such as 伺う. Short, clear commitments are useful in email.
grammar.example: 資料は午後にお送りします。
grammar.translation: I’ll send the materials this afternoon.

examples.ja: {資料|しりょう}は{午後|ごご}にお{送|おく}りします。
examples.en: I’ll send the materials this afternoon.

examples.ja: {結果|けっか}が{分|わ}かり{次第|しだい}、お{知|し}らせします。
examples.en: I’ll let you know as soon as the result is available.

examples.ja: {担当|たんとう}{者|しゃ}からお{電話|でんわ}します。
examples.en: The person in charge will call you.

grammar.mistake: Do not use お送りします to say the customer sends you a file. Name the actor when it is not obvious. お送りする is not the same perspective as お送りいただく.

grammar.title: State your side’s action formally
grammar.formation: ご + suitable する-verbal noun + いたす/いたします; お + suitable verb stem + いたす also occurs. ご説明いたします; お送りいたします.
grammar.explanation: いたす makes your side’s action a deferential statement to the listener. お/ご…いたす can also respect the person towards whom the act is directed. That combination is recognised usage, not automatically incorrect double keigo. In external email, 弊社 means our company and 貴社 commonly means your company; spoken 御社 is also respectful. Internal colleagues need not speak like external correspondence.
grammar.example: 弊社の担当者がご説明いたします。
grammar.translation: Our person in charge will explain it to you.

examples.ja: {弊社|へいしゃ}の{担当|たんとう}{者|しゃ}がご{説明|せつめい}いたします。
examples.en: Our person in charge will explain it to you.

examples.ja: {変更|へんこう}{点|てん}をご{案内|あんない}いたします。
{資料|しりょう}をお{送|おく}りいたします。
examples.en: I’ll send the materials to you.

grammar.mistake: For your action, use ご説明いたします, not ご説明なさいます. Do not add し after a する-verbal noun: ご説明しする is not this form.

grammar.title: Ask to perform an action yourself
grammar.formation: Verb causative て-form + いただく. 書く→書かせていただく; 見る→見させていただく; する→させていただく; 来る→来させていただく (こさせ). Question: …いただけますか.
grammar.explanation: You receive permission to carry out your own action, with a benefit or a felt benefit. In the scene, you ask to use the client’s supplied table in a proposal; the client can grant permission. In ご確認いただけますか the recipient checks; in 確認させていただけますか you ask to do the checking. This distinction is more useful than always choosing the longest wording. When permission is not relevant, a simple いたします statement may be clearer.
grammar.example: 頂いた表を提案書に使わせていただけますか。
grammar.translation: May I use the table you sent in the proposal?

examples.ja: {頂|いただ}いた{表|ひょう}を{提案|ていあん}{書|しょ}に{使|つか}わせていただけますか。
examples.en: May I use the table you sent in the proposal?

examples.ja: {許可|きょか}を{頂|いただ}いたので、{図|ず}を{使|つか}わせていただきました。
examples.en: I used the diagram with your permission.

examples.ja: {原本|げんぽん}を{確認|かくにん}させていただけますか。
examples.en: May I check the original document?

grammar.mistake: Do not confuse who acts. 確認させていただく concerns our checking; ご確認いただく concerns the recipient checking for us. Permission/benefit depend on context, not just status.

grammar.title: Request an action without deciding for the recipient
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + いただけますか/いただけませんか. Respectful regular form: お/ご + suitable stem + いただけますか. Extended business request: …いただけますでしょうか.
grammar.explanation: Acknowledge the effort, say what you need and leave the recipient a choice. ご確認いただけますか and ご確認いただけませんか are useful options. The extended いただけますでしょうか appears in business/service teaching materials; it is not universally wrong, nor automatically preferable. Put deadlines and alternatives clearly in the message. していただきます can present a settled arrangement rather than asking whether the recipient agrees.
grammar.example: お手数ですが、金曜の三時までにご返信いただけますか。
grammar.translation: Could you reply by three on Friday? Sorry for the trouble.

examples.ja: お{手数|てすう}ですが、{金曜|きんよう}の{三時|さんじ}までにご{返信|へんしん}いただけますか。
examples.en: Could you reply by three on Friday? Sorry for the trouble.

examples.ja: {難|むずか}しければ、ご{都合|つごう}をお{知|し}らせいただけませんか。
examples.en: If that’s difficult, could you let us know what works for you?

examples.ja: {添付|てんぷ}の{資料|しりょう}をご{確認|かくにん}いただけますでしょうか。
examples.en: Would you be able to check the attached materials?

grammar.mistake: Do not mark a shorter polite request wrong merely because the example uses でしょうか. Do not write ご確認させていただけますか when you mean to ask the recipient to check.

dialogues.title: Before the client email goes out
dialogues.scene: Mori and the learner check a draft brochure and its outgoing email. The client review is requested for Friday at three; four PDF pages are ready, but printing has not been ordered.

dialogues.title: Correct the date and ask about the table
dialogues.scene: The learner phones client Tamura after noticing a wrong weekday in an email. The actual visit is Thursday at two in the client’s second-floor meeting room. They also ask permission to include Tamura’s supplied table in the proposal.

lines.romaji: Tamura-san, mēru no nichiji ni goki ga arimashita. Mōshiwake arimasen.
lines.meaning: Tamura-san, there was an error in the date and time in my email. I’m sorry.

lines.meaning: It said Wednesday. It’s Thursday at two, right?

lines.meaning: Yes, Thursday at two. I’ll resend the corrected email.

lines.meaning: Understood. We’ll meet in our second-floor meeting room.

lines.meaning: Thank you. Mori and I will visit that day.

lines.romaji: Annai no pī dī efu mo todokimashita yo. Kinyō made ni mite okimasu.
lines.meaning: The brochure PDF arrived too. I’ll look through it by Friday.

readings.title: Correct the weekday, keep two deadlines separate
paragraphs: {件名|けんめい}：{訪問|ほうもん}{日時|にちじ}の{訂正|ていせい}と{資料|しりょう}の{再送|さいそう}。{田村|たむら}{様|さま}、いつもお{世話|せわ}になっております。バオです。{先|さき}ほどお{送|おく}りしたメールで、{訪問|ほうもん}の{曜日|ようび}を{水曜|すいよう}と{書|か}いてしまいました。{正|ただ}しくは{木曜|もくよう}の{午後|ごご}{二時|にじ}です。{混乱|こんらん}を{招|まね}き、{申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありません。

お{電話|でんわ}でご{確認|かくにん}いただいたとおり、{当日|とうじつ}は{森|もり}と{二人|ふたり}で{伺|うかが}います。{場所|ばしょ}は{貴社|きしゃ}の{二階|にかい}の{会議|かいぎ}{室|しつ}で、{所要|しょよう}{時間|じかん}は{三十分|さんじゅっぷん}を{予定|よてい}しております。{今回|こんかい}は{曜日|ようび}の{誤記|ごき}だけを{直|なお}しました。{時刻|じこく}や{場所|ばしょ}を{新|あたら}しく{変更|へんこう}したわけではありません。

{頂|いただ}いた{表|ひょう}は、{先|さき}ほどのご{了承|りょうしょう}に{基|もと}づき、{提案|ていあん}{書|しょ}に{使|つか}わせていただきます。{数字|すうじ}が{読|よ}めるよう、{表|ひょう}{全体|ぜんたい}を{大|おお}きく{載|の}せました。{修正|しゅうせい}した{資料|しりょう}を{添付|てんぷ}しておりますので、{木曜|もくよう}の{訪問|ほうもん}までにご{確認|かくにん}いただけますでしょうか。

{別|べつ}にお{送|おく}りした{案内|あんない}PDFへのご{返信|へんしん}は、{金曜|きんよう}の{午後|ごご}{三時|さんじ}までをお{願|ねが}いしております。この{資料|しりょう}と{案内|あんない}は{別|べつ}のものです。{同|おな}じ{期日|きじつ}ではありませんので、{件名|けんめい}をご{確認|かくにん}ください。もし{確認|かくにん}が{難|むずか}しい{場合|ばあい}は、お{電話|でんわ}でご{相談|そうだん}できればと{思|おも}います。お{手数|てすう}をおかけしますが、よろしくお{願|ねが}いいたします。バオ。

wrote it, with regret for the error

glosses.kana: ふたりでうかがいます

glosses.kana: ごきだけをなおしました

exercises.prompt: What does Mori ask to change before the PDF is sent?
options: Make the map lettering a little bigger
Delete all four pages
Change the client’s email address
exercises.explain: Mori says 地図の字だけ、もう少し大きくできますか.

exercises.prompt: What reply time is requested, subject to the client’s availability?
options: Three on Friday
Two on Thursday
Nine-thirty tonight
exercises.explain: The learner asks 金曜の三時まで; Mori says to ask about availability if that is difficult.

exercises.prompt: What should wait until the client review finishes?
options: Ordering the printing
Attaching the four-page PDF
Making the map lettering bigger
exercises.explain: Mori says 印刷はまだ頼まないでください.

exercises.context: Form practice: you will send the client the materials. Complete the お + ます-stem + します form.
options: お{送|おく}りします
お{送|おく}るします
お{送|おく}ってします
exercises.explain: 送り is the ます-stem of 送る; the speaker sends the materials.

exercises.context: Form practice: your person in charge explains to the client. Choose the regular ご…いたします form.
exercises.line: {弊社|へいしゃ}の{担当|たんとう}{者|しゃ}が＿＿。
options: ご{説明|せつめい}いたします
ご{説明|せつめい}しするします
ご{説明|せつめい}なさいます
exercises.explain: The action belongs to our side, not the customer. ご説明いたします combines recipient-directed respect with deferential speech.

exercises.context: You tell an external client that YOU will send the file this afternoon. Choose the wording that states your action respectfully.
exercises.line: {午後|ごご}にファイルを{送|おく}る。
options: {午後|ごご}にファイルをお{送|おく}りします。
{午後|ごご}にファイルをお{送|おく}りください。
{午後|ごご}にファイルをお{送|おく}りになります。
exercises.explain: お送りします states your sending. The other options request or honour the recipient’s sending, changing who acts.

exercises.meaning: Constrained form practice: say you will attach and send the materials.
exercises.explain: 添付して links attaching to your sending; this is one authored order.

exercises.prompt: What is attached to this review-request email?
options: The four-page brochure PDF
An invoice and a receipt
The original paper documents
exercises.explain: The first paragraph names all four pages; the third says it is not the quotation.

exercises.prompt: What is the status of the planned hundred copies?
options: Proposed; count and printing order follow the review
Already printed and delivered
Cancelled permanently
exercises.explain: 百部 is a plan, 決定 follows review and printing has not yet been ordered.

exercises.prompt: What should Tamura do if replying by Friday at three is difficult?
options: Tell Bao what timing works
Send paper originals instead
Pay an attached invoice immediately
exercises.explain: The second paragraph explicitly asks the client to say their availability.

exercises.prompt: Which visit is confirmed in the call?
options: Thursday at two, in the client’s second-floor meeting room
Wednesday at two, at the café
Friday at three, in Mori’s office
exercises.explain: Tamura and the learner confirm Thursday at two, then Tamura gives the room.

exercises.prompt: What does the learner ask permission to do?
options: Use the supplied table in the proposal
Ask Tamura to write a new table by tonight
Cancel the Thursday meeting
exercises.explain: The learner says 提案書に使わせていただけますか; the learner uses it.

exercises.prompt: What does Tamura ask about the table?
options: Make the numbers large enough to read
Remove all its numbers
Include only a tiny corner of it
exercises.explain: 数字が読める大きさにしてください states the condition.

exercises.context: Form practice: ask permission for YOU to use the client’s table. Use the causative て-form of 使う plus いただけますか.
options: {使|つか}わせていただけますか
{使|つか}わしているいただけますか
{使|つか}うさせていただけますか
exercises.explain: 使う becomes 使わせる, then 使わせて. Permission is for the speaker’s own use.

exercises.context: Form practice: ask the CLIENT to check the attached document. Choose the regular ご…いただけますか request.
exercises.line: {添付|てんぷ}の{資料|しりょう}を＿＿。
options: ご{確認|かくにん}いただけますか
ご{確認|かくにん}させていただけますか
ご{確認|かくにん}いただきます
exercises.explain: The recipient checks for you. させていただく asks for your checking; いただきます presents it as arranged rather than asks.

exercises.context: You need an external client to reply to a request. They have not agreed yet. Choose a respectful request that leaves them a choice.
exercises.line: {金曜|きんよう}までに{返信|へんしん}する。
options: お{手数|てすう}ですが、{金曜|きんよう}までにご{返信|へんしん}いただけますか。
{金曜|きんよう}までに{絶対|ぜったい}{返信|へんしん}してね。
{金曜|きんよう}までにご{返信|へんしん}いただくことに{決|き}めました。
exercises.explain: The first asks and acknowledges effort; the others demand or unilaterally decide the client’s action. Other clear polite requests are also valid.

tiles: ご{了承|りょうしょう}を
{使|つか}わせていただきます
exercises.meaning: Constrained form practice: put the permission first, then say you will use the table with it.
exercises.explain: The established permission supports the speaker’s subsequent use. This is one authored order.

exercises.prompt: What was corrected rather than newly changed?
options: The written weekday; the actual time and place are unchanged
The actual visit time moved from two to three
The meeting moved from the client to the café
exercises.explain: The second paragraph distinguishes correcting 誤記 from changing time or place.

exercises.prompt: Which review timing belongs to which document?
options: Proposal before Thursday’s visit; brochure reply by Friday at three
Both documents by Friday at three
Brochure before Wednesday; proposal next month
exercises.explain: The last two paragraphs distinguish the proposal from the separately sent brochure.

exercises.prompt: Why can Bao use the table in the proposal?
options: Tamura already granted permission in the call
Bao assumes silence means agreement
The table was newly created by Mori
exercises.explain: 先ほどのご了承に基づき refers back to the explicit permission.

recycling.reason: The work conversation checks a brochure, a mistaken weekday and permission for a table. Only earlier terms actually present in this setting count. News and venue vocabulary is not padded into client correspondence to reach a percentage.

grammar: our action お〜する/ご〜いたす
own action with permission させていただく
recipient request いただけますか
watch.prompt: Optionally read a real email you can use. Identify the sender’s promised action, the recipient’s requested action, a date, and any alternative if that timing is difficult. Save useful complete phrases in context.
